claims.explanation: Deforolimus is an allosteric mTORC1 inhibitor (rapalog), so sensitivity is expected in tumors whose growth depends on mTORC1-driven translation downstream of PI3K/AKT activation. The strongest selective-killing pattern is enrichment for PTEN loss-of-function and PIK3CA mutation/activation, which relieve negative regulation of PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 and create pathway addiction; this is supported by the known role of PTEN loss and PI3K amplification/mutation in mTOR-pathway deregulation and by the observed enrichment of PTEN-mutant and PIK3CA-mutant lines among the most killed lines.

features.basis: PTEN loss activates PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 and is a canonical mTOR-inhibitor sensitivity marker; PTEN-mutant lines (OVK18, SF295, ZR751, SF126, MFE319) are enriched among the most killed lines
Activating PIK3CA mutations drive PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 signaling; PIK3CA-mutant lines (RT112, HCC1954, HGC27, MFE319) are enriched among the most killed lines
MTOR pathway alterations, including MTOR mutation, can create dependence on mTORC1 signaling; MFE319 (MTOR-mutant) is among the most killed lines
AKT activation downstream of PI3K is a reported mTOR-pathway deregulation event and would predict rapalog sensitivity
Loss of PI3K regulatory subunit relieves inhibition of PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 signaling, analogous to PTEN loss
STK11/LKB1 loss activates AMPK-independent survival and is associated with resistance to mTORC1 inhibition; STK11-mutant lines (NCIH1623, PLCPRF5, G361, NCIH1915) appear in both tails, weakening this
KRAS-mutant tumors often bypass mTORC1 dependence through MAPK-driven translation; KRAS-mutant lines (GSU, SNU81, TCCPAN2, SW1573, T3M4) are enriched among least affected lines
NRAS-mutant melanoma/glioma lines (IPC298, SW1088, SNU719) include least-affected lines, suggesting MAPK activation reduces rapalog sensitivity
BRAF-mutant lines appear in both tails (AM38, G361, MFE319 killed; UACC62 least affected), so BRAF mutation alone is weak and likely context-dependent
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK signaling, which can bypass mTORC1 dependence; NF1-mutant lines appear in both tails, making this weak evidence
TP53 mutation is nearly ubiquitous across both tails and therefore not selective; included only to note lack of discriminating value
CDKN2A loss is common in both tails and does not track with selective killing
